clue.text: Supports rector going down and stops

indicators.note: going means leaving, so the rector's letter comes out of its place in the supports word
in a down clue, down means the letter is put back lower in the word

parts.note: bras are supports worn as underwear

explanation.surface: A rector moves on, both supporting things and putting a stop to them.
explanation.walkthrough: In BRAS, the R (rector) slides one place further down the light, past the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar is to block or prohibit, so 'bars' as a verb means stops.

clue.text: Prisoner associated with tower plot

parts.note: con is short for convict
a spire is a tall pointed tower on a church

explanation.surface: A prisoner in a tower hatching an escape plan, as in a historical drama.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to scheme secretly together, a verb synonym of plot.

clue.text: Bishop and President having a tot

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president

explanation.surface: A bishop and a president sharing a drink together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small measure of spirits to share, but it is a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: A babe is an infant, and a tot is a small child, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Emperor is in Madrid hosting queen and other rulers

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a tsar was the Russian emperor
Qu. is an abbreviation for queen
es is Spanish for is

explanation.surface: A visiting emperor in Madrid entertains a queen and other monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: The emperor holds the queen; the Spanish word follows. 'Rulers' looks like monarchs after the emperor and queen, but means drawing instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-square is a drafting ruler shaped like a T, so these are rulers of another kind than monarchs.

clue.text: Crosses jaw, that hurts seriously in the face

parts.note: to jaw and to yak both mean to chatter
ow is the cry when something hurts

indicators.note: the face is the front, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: first letter of seriously

explanation.surface: Someone crosses swords verbally, and a blow to the jaw really hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crosses' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: hybrid animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A yakow is a hybrid bred from a yak and a domestic cow, so yakows are crosses.

clue.text: Maybe 8 block freezer

parts.note: a cube is a solid block, like an ice cube
read as numb-er, something that makes numb

explanation.surface: A block of ice from the freezer, perhaps eight of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freezer' is read as something that numbs, a numb-er.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is two multiplied by itself three times, so it is an example of a perfect cube.

clue.text: A rook is not so present around New England

indicators.note: around says one word wraps itself about the other

parts.note: to host a show is to present it
NE is the abbreviation for New England

explanation.surface: A chess rook is absent from a game set in New England.
explanation.walkthrough: A rook is a swindler, so whatever a rook is not is honest.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to cheat them, so a rook is dishonest and its opposite is honest.

clue.text: Kite maybe caught for English composer

indicators.note: caught is used as in caught by the ear, heard rather than read

parts.note: a kite is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: The setter, Kite, is caught out naming an English composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Kite is also this puzzle's setter. William Byrd was the leading Tudor composer.
explanation.definitionFit: William Byrd was a Renaissance English composer of church and keyboard music.

clue.text: Popular Omani covered up nose

indicators.note: something covered up lies concealed inside the words around it

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A well-liked man from Oman covered up his nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nose is the wine-taster's word for a bouquet or smell, so aroma is a synonym.

clue.text: Trim bust in front of Conservative having come to be expected

indicators.note: trimming cuts a little off the end

parts.note: a bust is a sculpture, a kind of statue
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician whose bust has had a trim, as was expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutory can mean regular and customary, as in a statutory appearance, something come to be expected.

clue.text: Prolonged emergency — the last part of 6 breaking out

parts.note: SOS is the distress call used in an emergency
the answer to 6 ends in TEN, its last part

indicators.note: breaking means broken up, so the letters of out are rearranged

explanation.surface: A long crisis with the end of another clue escaping.
explanation.walkthrough: SOS, then TEN from the end of 6, then UTO from the broken-up word out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sostenuto is a musical direction meaning sustained, the notes held for their full value.

clue.text: Repair an electronic item? Correct

parts.note: E as in e-mail stands for electronic
to mend is to repair

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to fix a gadget and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as e-mend: repairing an electronic item.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct its errors, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: 'More unusual' place of learning associated with queen, earl and king

parts.note: uni is short for university
Qu. is an abbreviation for queen
E abbreviates earl
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A university with royal and noble connections is rather out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniquer is a comparative form of unique, so it means more one-of-a-kind or unusual.

clue.text: Posh knight better remove hat

parts.note: U means upper-class
N is the chess notation for knight
to cap something is to outdo or better it

explanation.surface: A posh knight had better doff his hat.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a long-standing British label for posh usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncap is to take the cap off, so it means to remove a hat.

clue.text: Make clear that engineer can slumber

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or contrive, so the letters are rebuilt into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to rework

explanation.surface: Explaining that an engineer is able to doze.
explanation.definitionFit: To unscramble a message is to sort it out so it becomes intelligible, that is to make it clear.

clue.text: Blind Faith ultimately deliver when following Sabbath

parts.note: S abbreviates sabbath

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so just the final letter is taken

parts.note: final letter of faith
to utter a speech is to deliver it

explanation.surface: The rock band Blind Faith plays after Black Sabbath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blind' and 'Faith' read as the band, but split: Blind is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shutter is a window cover that blocks light, the same as a blind.

clue.text: Heating enabled with this element

parts.note: rad is short for radiator, a heating device
a switched-on device is enabled

explanation.surface: The heating has been turned on with this chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas, one of the chemical elements.

clue.text: It involves mate getting companion to accompany letter

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour
ess is the spelt name of the letter S

explanation.surface: A friend gets a companion to go with a letter to the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like a friend, but it is checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: The game of chess is won by checkmate, so a game that involves mate.

clue.text: Remove short pocket

indicators.note: short means cut off before its end

parts.note: to sack someone is to remove them from a job

explanation.surface: An instruction to take out a short pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A sac is a pouch-like cavity in a body or plant, essentially a pocket.

clue.text: Charlie perhaps with a scruffy yak being ancient Indian polymath

parts.note: Charlie Chan is a fictional Chinese-American detective, so Chan is one surname of a Charlie

indicators.note: scruffy means untidy, so the letters of yak are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fellow called Charlie with a scruffy yak, cast as an Indian sage.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAN, A, then KYA from scrambling YAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanakya was a teacher, philosopher and royal adviser of ancient India, credited with the Arthashastra.

clue.text: Mount of dictator's fed up

indicators.note: a dictator here is one who dictates, speaking words for someone to write down

parts.note: being fed up is being weary and uninterested

explanation.surface: A dictator's horse is tired of it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' looks like a tyrant, but means someone dictating out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: To board a ship or train is to get on it, as mount means to get on a horse.

clue.text: Functions as nice Royal Society assembly

indicators.note: an assembly puts parts together into something new, so these letters are constructed afresh

parts.note: taken as written
RS is the abbreviation for the Royal Society

explanation.surface: A meeting of the Royal Society goes off as nicely as can be.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcsine is the inverse trigonometric function of sine, so arcsines are mathematical functions.

clue.text: A prior revolutionary queen is like some Ba'athists

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests overturning, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Q is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A revolutionary former queen sides with political radicals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ba'ath party ruled Iraq under Saddam Hussein, so many of its members supported Iraq.

clue.text: Writer absorbed by dictionary spread out

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken inside another thing

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
a pen is a writing tool

explanation.surface: An author engrossed in a dictionary spread open on the desk.
explanation.definitionFit: Opened means unfolded or laid open, so a map opened is spread out.

clue.text: Repeatedly, starts to quietly walk around former 25 homeland

indicators.note: repeatedly means those three opening letters are written down twice
the starts of the next three words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Someone keeps walking softly around an old homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes QWA from 'quietly walk around'; 'Repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: QwaQwa was a black homeland set up by apartheid South Africa, abolished in 1994.

clue.text: Continental fair refurbished toilet

indicators.note: refurbished means done up again, so the letters of fair are reworked

parts.note: can is American slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A tidy toilet that has been refitted, on the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continental' suggests mainland Europe, but here it is the adjective for one particular continent.
explanation.definitionFit: African describes things from Africa, which is a continent, so it is one sense of continental.

clue.text: A plank across a ship

parts.note: taken as written
a beam is a long piece of timber

explanation.surface: A plank laid over a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam is a nautical term for at right angles to a ship's length, that is across it.

clue.text: Bohemian, gutless and irritable

indicators.note: gutless means having the insides removed, so the central letter goes

parts.note: artsy means arty and bohemian

explanation.surface: A description of a spineless, grumpy bohemian.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsy is British slang for bad-tempered and awkward, a synonym of irritable.

clue.text: One who investigates figures has stamina to be exercised

indicators.note: exercising works and moves things around, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rework

explanation.surface: A fitness researcher whose stamina must be put through its paces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' looks like numbers, but it means bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomist studies the structure of bodies, and figures can mean human forms.

clue.text: It's an honour to hold doctor's second instrument

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: second asks for the letter in position two of the word

parts.note: the letter in second place of doctor

explanation.surface: Being awarded an honour while playing a doctor's second instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Slice served up for gin

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a slice is a part or portion

explanation.surface: A slice of lemon served with a gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' looks like the drink, but it is a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is an old word for a snare used to catch animals, that is a trap.

clue.text: Sneak off but stop around back of castle in the style of William the First

indicators.note: around says one word wraps the others inside it

parts.note: to stay is to stop or remain

indicators.note: the back is the tail end, so only the final letter is taken

parts.note: final letter of castle
à la is French for in the style of

indicators.note: first picks just the opening letter of the name

parts.note: first letter of William

explanation.surface: Sneaking away from a castle like William the Conqueror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'William the First' suggests the Conqueror, but it only asks for his initial.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal away is to leave quietly and secretly, that is to sneak off.

clue.text: Macbeth possibly makes comeback in Shakespeare poem

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the letters are read in the backward direction
in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the tail of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Macbeth returns inside a Shakespeare poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth suggests the play, but Verdi also wrote an opera of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Macbeth is an opera, so Macbeth is possibly an example of one.
